3.why: 90, 60, 15 are a family of standard multiples of 15; 144 is the lone member outside it and the lone perfect square.

4.why: 21 is the derivational hub - 21/3=7, 21/7=3, 21/4=5.25 - so the other three are all simple transforms of it.

5.why: 12, 24, 36 is a three-term arithmetic (and 1:2:3) run with 26 as the outlier; I take the middle term of the run.

6.why: Two perfectly symmetric sign-flip pairs (+/-11, +/-43) with nothing to separate them.

7.why: 30, 60, 80 are a family of multiples of ten; 48 is the lone member outside the family.

8.why: 36 is the hub of the related family (36/4=9, 36x2=72), and 5 is unrelated to everything so cannot be the source of these distractors.

9.why: Two competing magnitude relations (200/2000 a factor-of-ten pair, 2000/3000 vs 18000) leave no single hub.

10.why: 8, 9, 10 is a three-term arithmetic run with 4 as the outlier; I take the middle term.

14.why: 2/5 is the hub: 4/25 is its square, 4/5 its double, 1/10 its quarter - all three are derived from it.

15.why: 3, 7, 11, 15 is a complete four-term arithmetic run with no outlier and no distinguished member.

16.why: A complete 2x2 cross product of x in {3,11} and y in {2,6}; perfectly balanced.

17.why: $45.00 is the lone round figure and $12.50 the magnitude outlier, narrowing to A/B, but nothing separates $46.80 from $100.80.

20.why: Two tight pairs three apart (6/9 and 46/49) in a fully symmetric arrangement.

21.why: 7, 14, 42 are a multiples-of-7 family with 12 outside it, but the three are tied on relation count so the choice within the family is unsupported.

22.why: The lone decimal (3.5) and the lone negative (-2) are both classic slip distractors, leaving 6 and 4 with nothing to separate them.

23.why: Additively closed set (2+5=7, 5+7=12) where 5 and 7 are tied as hubs.

24.why: 9 is the hub with a relation to every other option: 9/2=4.5, 9x6=54, 9/3=3.

25.why: Two ratios each given in both orders (2:3, 3:2, 3:5, 5:3) - perfectly symmetric, nothing leaks.

26.why: 150 is the lone round value in a tight cluster (I bet round-in-a-cluster is bait), but 147/149/152 are not otherwise separable.

27.why: 2500 and 2400 are round estimate-bait; 2652 and 2448 are 2550 plus/minus 4% and equally derived, so the pick between them is unsupported.

28.why: -5 is the lone negative (sign-error bait), but 17, 23, 41 form no run and no hub.

29.why: 23 is a magnitude outlier, leaving 5, 8, 9 which are not an arithmetic run, so 8 is only loosely central.

30.why: 2, 4, 6, 8 is a complete four-term arithmetic run with no outlier - a clean set.
